_info.comment: Fork identifiers for Hoodi, a proof-of-stake testnet merged at genesis. It carries the one case in this family where the genesis-timestamp filter changes the answer.
_info.aForkDeclaredAtTimestampZERO: Hoodi's configuration declares a fork at timestamp 0. It contributes NOTHING to the checksum: the reference client drops every fork time at or below the genesis timestamp, and this network's genesis is 1,742,212,800. A client that accumulates each declared timestamp without that filter produces a wrong identifier at the very first vector and will not peer. No other network in this family exercises it.
_info.thisNetworkHasZeroBlockBasedBoundaries: Like Holesky, every fork here is a timestamp and there is no block dimension at all.
_info.mergedAtGenesis: Terminal total difficulty of exactly zero, and a MergeNetsplitBlock of zero which is likewise dropped as the genesis ruleset. There was no proof-of-work phase.
_info.genesisTimestampFiltersTheSchedule: A fork identifier accumulates only timestamps STRICTLY GREATER than the genesis block's own timestamp -- the reference client drops the rest as 'forks before genesis'. This network's genesis timestamp is 1742212800. That filter is load-bearing here: the configuration declares a fork at timestamp 0, which is dropped, so a client that accumulates every declared timestamp produces a wrong identifier from the very first vector.
_info.oracle: Two independent sources agreeing. Computed from EIP-2124 and EIP-6122, and cross-checked against go-ethereum's OWN published table for this network, PARSED FROM ITS SOURCE rather than transcribed -- all 10 published cases reproduce.
_info.oracle-version: go-ethereum, params/config.go HoodiChainConfig, core/genesis.go and core/forkid/forkid_test.go
_info.useYourOwnGenesisHash: Seed from the genesis hash YOUR client computes; the one here is a cross-check. Taken the other way every vector passes regardless of what genesis was built.
